title: Agent Certificate v0 Signature and Co-Attestation Wire Shapes
description: Issuer-signature scope and client co-attestation block for Agent Certificate v0, per C6 Ruling 3(iv) (reconciled, binding): 'the client signs a canonical unsigned-manifest digest covering subject, seal, complete claims and tiers, evidence digests, mandatory NON-claims, privacy mode, SDK identity, compiler/register versions, key/ring identifiers, and freshness data. The issuer then signs that manifest and the client signature.' Spine-digest-only binding was OVERTURNED: 'signing only the spine, privacy mode, SDK identity, and nonce allows the issuer to attach a different claim set, tiers, evidence references, and NON-claims to the same client signature.' This family does NOT reuse ArtifactSignatureEnvelopeV2 — reuse was struck ('not established merely because the existing KMS key matches that envelope. Adding nested signatures and new fields changes the format and verifier'). The v0 issuer path is a new dedicated per-environment certificate-signing key through protected GitHub-OIDC CI (C6 Ruling 4); the trust ring must be a signed, versioned artifact whose root fingerprint is pinned in the independent verifier, failing closed for unknown keys — a mutable ConfigMap is transport only, never authority. Root instance is one CertificateSignaturesV0.

UnsignedManifestCoverageV0.description: The FIXED coverage list of the canonical unsigned manifest — the eleven sections C6 Ruling 3(iv) enumerates, pinned as a const so a manifest that covers less is unrepresentable. Freshness data is covered material; per-certificate expiry semantics are pinned by the signed semantics manifest.

UnsignedManifestRefV0.description: Reference to the canonical unsigned manifest: its digest plus the pinned coverage list. The digest is computed over the canonical serialization defined by the signed semantics manifest; 'A digest without an archived, authentic bundle and resolver does not preserve verification' (C1 Ruling 6) — archival is a B5/verifier obligation this shape cannot discharge.

CoAttestationV0.description: The client co-attestation block. The client signs the FULL canonical unsigned-manifest digest (never a spine digest). Scope carried verbatim from C6 Ruling 3(iv): 'That does not mean the client attests every server assertion as true; it means the client attests that these are the exact bytes it co-signed.' The client key crosses as an OpaqueRef, not a raw public key — tension T3 (print the key, a blinded reference, or nothing) is unresolved between C6 and C1; the linkability-conservative opaque-reference encoding is used pending a Disclosure Register entry for the co-attestation key material (C1 Ruling 5, client->server entry 3).

client_key_ref.description: Opaque reference to the enrolled client signing key. A stable pseudonymous identifier with a linkability cost (C1, tension T3); never raw public-key bytes in v0.

signed_manifest_digest.description: MUST equal the unsigned manifest's manifest_digest; the envelope binds the two (mismatch is the co-attestation-mismatch fixture class).

nonce.description: Public anti-replay nonce. Register entry 8 wording travels verbatim: a public nonce 'does not prevent dictionary guessing.'

IssuerSignatureV0.description: The issuer signature. Signing order is conceded and binding: 'issuer signature should cover the client signature bytes' — signed_payload names exactly what the issuer signed, and the enclosing CertificateSignaturesV0 forces the covering form whenever a co-attestation is present. The signing workflow 'must verify the finalized manifest and ledger before signing' (C6 Ruling 4); that is a B5 obligation recorded here as scope, not proven by this shape.

issuer_key_ref.description: Opaque reference to the dedicated per-environment certificate-signing key. Never the development Planner key; the general backend pod holds no certificate-signing authority (C6 Ruling 4, binding).

trust_ring_ref.description: Opaque reference to the signed, versioned trust-ring artifact (with version) under which the issuer key is published. Offline verification additionally needs 'a compiled minimum checkpoint or another pinned release policy' against rollback (C6 Ruling 4) — a verifier obligation, not representable here.

signed_payload.description: Exactly what the issuer signed: the unsigned manifest alone, or the unsigned manifest plus the client co-attestation bytes.

CertificateSignaturesV0.description: The complete signature block: canonical unsigned-manifest reference, optional client co-attestation, and the issuer signature. When a co-attestation is present the issuer signature MUST cover it (signed_payload = [unsigned_manifest, co_attestation]); when absent it MUST NOT claim to. 'Missing co-attestation should refuse issuance' for any tier-1 claim — that refusal is enforced at the certificate envelope (tier-1 claims require this block's co_attestation), not silently downgraded.
